info.title: Partner API
info.description: Provision your customers, sign them in with single sign-on, issue their workspace API keys and connect their social accounts and messaging channels. Authenticated by your partner key as `X-API-KEY`, from your backend only.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Create or refresh a customer's account and workspace.

tags.name: Single sign-on
tags.description: Swap a token signed with your SSO secret for a one-time sign-in link.

tags.name: Workspace API keys
tags.description: Issue, list and revoke the `osk_` keys of a workspace you provisioned.

tags.name: Client Connect API
tags.description: Hosted links that connect, or reconnect, a customer's social accounts and messaging channels, WhatsApp and Telegram included. One endpoint for every provider.

post.description: Creates the customer's account and a workspace of their own, or refreshes a customer you provisioned before. Safe to repeat. An e-mail that already belongs to someone else is never taken over: it is a `409` with an `error_code`, and nothing is written. See [Single sign-on](/partner/single-sign-on#1-provision-the-customer).

external_id.description: Your own id for the customer. Use something that never changes.

get.description: A customer you provisioned, with their workspaces.

post.description: Swaps a token you signed with HS256 and your SSO secret (claims `sub` = the customer's `external_id`, `email`, optional `name`, and a short `exp`) for a sign-in link that works once, within 5 minutes. A `sub` that was never provisioned is provisioned first. No partner key is sent. 20 requests a minute per client address. See [Single sign-on](/partner/single-sign-on).

authentication_url.description: Send the customer's browser here. Add `redirect` to choose where they land.

400.description: Missing parameters, or the token was rejected: expired, wrong signature, missing `email`, an e-mail mismatch or domain restriction, or a provisioning conflict.

get.description: The workspace's keys, including ones an admin made in the dashboard. Never the secret.

post.description: Creates an `osk_` key for the workspace. `plain_text_token` is returned **once** and cannot be retrieved again. A permission the workspace cannot have is a `422`. At most 25 live keys per workspace, shared with the dashboard.

expires_at.description: A future time, or `null` for no expiry.

message.example: API key created. The token is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.

delete.description: Revokes the key immediately, for every API. Repeating it returns `200`.

message.example: API key revoked for all products.

get.description: Whether the Client Connect API is on for you, which providers can be connected, and your registered return URLs.

entities.description: Your customer ticks accounts after signing in.

configured.description: `false`: not set up yet; a link fails at the start with `provider_not_configured`.

asks_for.description: What the hosted page asks for when you did not send it; `bot_token` for Telegram.

put.description: Replaces your return URLs. Up to 20 HTTPS URLs, without credentials, query strings or fragments. Matching is exact, including the path and any trailing slash. Removing a URL also stops unfinished sessions from completing against it.

get.description: How many more publishing accounts the workspace's plan allows, and per provider whether a new one may be started now. WhatsApp numbers and Telegram bots have their own limits, checked when they are stored, so they read `true`.

post.description: Starts a 30-minute session and returns `connect_url`. Open it as a top-level navigation in your customer's browser, never in an iframe or a fetch. `account_id` or `channel_id` makes it a reconnect. For `telegram` send `bot_token` instead of `return_url`: the bot is connected in this call and the connection comes back `connected`, with `meta.webhook_registered` and `meta.webhook_taken_over` (`201` for a new bot, `200` for the same bot again). See [Client Connect API](/partner/client-connect).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1–200 characters. The same key and request returns the same connection with `200`; a different request on that key is a `409`. Not used for Telegram.

return_url.description: One of your registered return URLs, exactly. Required for every provider but `telegram`.

state.description: Comes back on the return URL and in the completion events. No secrets or personal data.

account_id.description: Reconnect this publishing account (of that workspace and provider).

channel_id.description: Reconnect this messaging channel: a WhatsApp channel, or a channel that belongs to an account of `provider`.

coexistence.description: `whatsapp` only: keep the number on the WhatsApp Business app.

max_accounts.description: Providers with a picker: the most accounts your customer may tick.

allow_unverified.description: Reconnects: let your customer confirm a profile that cannot be proven to be the same one.

server.description: `mastodon`: the server. Asked on the hosted page when absent.

handle.description: `blue_sky`: the handle Bluesky's sign-in opens on.

bot_token.description: `telegram` only: the BotFather token. Never stored on the connection or echoed back.

takeover.description: `telegram` only: move the bot's webhook here even though it points somewhere else.

200.description: The connection this Idempotency-Key already made, or the same Telegram bot again

403.description: The Client Connect API is not on for you.

409.description: The Idempotency-Key was used for a different request.

get.description: The authoritative result of a session. Read it when your customer comes back to your return URL.

post.description: Cancels an unfinished session. Safe to repeat, and never disconnects an account or channel that already connected.

get.description: The workspace's messaging channels. Public fields only, never channel data or tokens.
One messaging channel. Public fields only.

partnerKey.name: X-API-KEY
partnerKey.description: Your partner API key, `pk_…`. Backend only.

Workspace.name: workspace
Workspace.description: A workspace uuid from provisioning. It must be administered by a customer you provisioned.

workspace_id.description: The customer's first workspace, which provisioning created. `null` if they administer none.

workspace_ids.description: Every workspace the customer administers, oldest first.

prefix.description: The first characters of the key, to recognise it.

id.description: The integer the Publishing API's post endpoints take in `accounts`.
The integer the Publishing API's post endpoints take in `accounts`.

accounts.description: Every account connected, a WhatsApp number included.

channel_id.description: The messaging channel, when there is one.

connect_url.description: Only on a pending, unexpired session. A one-session capability: hand it straight to the customer's browser and never log it.

NotFound.description: Not found, or not yours. Another partner's workspace and a uuid that does not exist look the same.

Conflict.description: The e-mail belongs to someone else. Nothing was written.

example.message: That email address is already in use.

Refused.description: Refused, for example an e-mail outside your allowed domains.

example.message: Email domain not allowed for this partner.
